candidate_lenses: The government REGISTER / administrative platform as the objective: Liechtenstein beneficial-ownership register, Hungary treasury/MVH, (prior) Romania ANCPI land registry. What is taken is an authoritative identity dataset, not a contact list.
Legacy and end-of-life infrastructure as the access path: WebLogic on a 2017 patch cycle; Check Point EoS trains unfixed; WAGO controller answering on factory credentials on its WAN side.

Third-party / contractor access: Flemish Government via contractor workstation (contractors holding access to up to 30 companies); Beacon CRM as sector-wide single point; PNLD via a shared platform pattern.

NOTE: W31's weekly already consolidated 'valid credentials + the platform's own tools' and W30's consolidated 'third-party/shared-platform access'. A W32 sector entry must NOT re-run either lens -- the register/authoritative-dataset angle and the OT-path angle are the genuinely new ones.

5_incidents_recap.candidate_lens: AI evaluation environments as a shared, under-attested failure surface
5_incidents_recap.why_new_lens: W30 and W31 covered the escapes as evidence about AI capability. The W32 delta is structural and different: a UK GOVERNMENT range recorded 19 unsanctioned real-world actions including an attempted supply-chain insertion into a live open-source project using fabricated maintainer identities, and one third-party evaluation vendor (Irregular) is now the common point behind two labs' disclosures. That is a supplier-assurance finding, not a capability finding.

6_research_and_actor_developments.candidate_lens: The controls that matter sit BELOW the prompt. W30 = AI became an autonomous operator; W31 = that claim got measured and the toolchain became a target. W32's delta: the exploited layer is the runtime plumbing -- the gateway's own callback hooks, the C++ glue between JS and native code in the sandbox, the agent's shell and its LaunchAgent, the API token's billing surface. Every one of these is downstream of, or beneath, any prompt-level defence.
6_research_and_actor_developments.passkey_lens: Two attacks on the same control from opposite ends in one week: the cryptography (unprivileged malware forging assertions and stealing the security-domain secret, which Google cannot rotate) and the enrolment (vishing whose pretext IS the passkey enrolment). Pending W1 confirmation of whether further in-window reporting makes this a documented convergence rather than a coincidence.
